newsitem.title: USA: Arctic temps drive NYMEX Hub natgas up sharply.
newsitem.headline: Arctic temps drive NYMEX Hub natgas up sharply.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Monday in an active session, driven by forecasts for some Arctic-like U.S. temperatures later this week and next, industry sources said.
Spot-February surged 53 cents to close at $3.636 per million British thermal units. March settled 41.1 cents higher at $3.205. Other contracts ended up by 2.5 to 15 cents.

"It's all weather right now. We've got some cold weather coming, and I think we're going higher," said one Houston-based trader, adding even Texas temperatures were expected to dive to below freezing later this week.

Spot futures, which jumped 17 percent Monday, gapped sharply higher on the open and never looked back, as reports of an Arctic mass descending from Canada into the Midwest again roused the bulls. Technical factors also contributed to the rally, which began midweek last week after a 32 percent slide around the Christmas holiday.

Forecasters were calling for well below-normal Midwest temperatures this week, with the cold expected to dip into Texas later in the week. Eastern temperatures also were expected to dive by late week.
Technically, traders now pegged February resistance in the $3.90s and then at the contract high of $4.02. Support was seen first in Monday's $3.11-3.45 gap and then in the $2.60s.

Physical gas price gains Monday outpaced futures, with the Gulf Coast rallying almost 90 cents to the $3.45 to $3.50 area. Midcon pipes surged on the cold by more than $1.30 to the $3.65-3.70 range. Gas at the New York city gate gained 50 cents to about $4.00.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 12.7 cents to $2.54.
NYMEX Alberta natgas did not trade Monday.
NYMEX March Permian natgas ended 20 cents higher at a new contract high of $2.55, while other months were untraded.

On the KCBT, February closed up 60 cents at $3.50, while deferreds finished 3.5 to 54.0 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by seven cents to 13.6 cents (NYMEX premium). ((J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
